statement: Find all solutions in $0\le x<2\pi$ of the equation $\sin x+\sin3x+\sin5x=0$.
solution: Using $\sin x+\sin5x=2\sin3x\cos2x$, the equation becomes $\sin3x(2\cos2x+1)=0$. Either $\sin3x=0$, giving $3x=k\pi$ so $x=0,\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\pi,\tfrac{4\pi}{3},\tfrac{5\pi}{3}$; or $2\cos2x+1=0$, i.e. $\cos2x=-\tfrac12$, giving $2x=\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\tfrac{4\pi}{3},\tfrac{8\pi}{3},\tfrac{10\pi}{3}$ so $x=\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\tfrac{4\pi}{3},\tfrac{5\pi}{3}$. The full set is $x=0,\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\pi,\tfrac{4\pi}{3},\tfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
hints: Pair $\sin x$ and $\sin5x$ with a sum-to-product identity.
